Narayana Guru–SNDP 1903–Kerala; Periyar–Self-Respect 1925; Ambedkar–Mahad 1927.

subtopics.title: Congress, Moderates & Extremists (1885–1916)
subtopics.concept: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885. Its first leaders, the Moderates, asked the British for reforms through petitions. The Extremists wanted self-rule and used mass protest. From 1905 to 1916 came the Bengal partition, a Congress split, separate electorates and Home Rule.

tricks.title: Five-six-seven-nine: "Split, League, Split, Separate"
tricks.body: **1905** Bengal split → **1906** Muslim League → **1907** Congress split (Surat) → **1909** separate electorates (Morley–Minto).

example.q: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced by:
steps: Separate electorates = the "9" in 5-6-7-9.
1909 = Morley–Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act).

mistakes.wrong: Putting the Surat split in 1905.
mistakes.right: Surat split = **1907**. 1905 is the Bengal partition.

mistakes.wrong: Calling Tilak Gandhi's political guru.
mistakes.right: Gandhi's political guru was the Moderate **Gokhale**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the Lucknow Pact (1916) was between Moderates and Extremists only.
mistakes.right: The pact was between the **Congress and the Muslim League**. The two Congress wings also reunited there.

mistakes.wrong: Naming A.O. Hume the first Congress president.
mistakes.right: Hume organised it. The first president was **W.C. Bonnerjee**.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing Lajpat Rai's *Young India* with Gandhi's.
mistakes.right: Lajpat Rai's *Young India* is a **book**. Gandhi's *Young India* is a **journal**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Besant's Home Rule League came first.
mistakes.right: **Tilak's** came first (April 1916). Besant's came in September 1916.

subtopics.notes:
### The Congress is born (1885)
**A.O. Hume**, a retired British civil servant, called 72 Indian delegates to **Bombay**. They met at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College on **28 December 1885**. This was the first session of the **Indian National Congress (INC)**. The first president was **W.C. Bonnerjee**. The Viceroy was **Dufferin**.

Some said Hume wanted a "safety valve" to let out Indian anger. **Lala Lajpat Rai** argued this in his book *Young India*. Modern historians see the Congress as the first all-India political platform.

> **Watch:** The founder-organiser (Hume) was British. The first president (Bonnerjee) was Indian.

### The Moderates (1885–1905)
Moderates used petitions, prayers and protests, the "3P" method. They trusted British justice.

| Leader | Remember for |
|---|---|
| **Dadabhai Naoroji** | "Grand Old Man of India"; president three times; first Indian MP in the British House of Commons (1892); **Drain of Wealth** theory in *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* (1901) |
| **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** | Servants of India Society (1905); **Gandhi's political guru** |
| **Surendranath Banerjea** | Indian Association (1876); paper *Bengalee* |
| Pherozeshah Mehta | "Lion of Bombay" |
| R.C. Dutt | *Economic History of India* |

The **drain of wealth** means India's money flowed to Britain as salaries, pensions and profits.

### The Extremists (1905–1919)
Extremists wanted self-rule (swaraj), not petitions. They used mass action, swadeshi and national education.
- **Lal-Bal-Pal:** **Lala Lajpat Rai** ("Punjab Kesari"), **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, **Bipin Chandra Pal** (Bengal). **Aurobindo Ghosh** joined them.
- **Tilak:** papers *Kesari* (Marathi) and *Mahratta* (English). Started the **Ganapati (1893)** and **Shivaji (1895)** festivals.
- Tilak's slogan: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it."**
- Tilak was jailed in **Mandalay** (1908–14), where he wrote *Gita Rahasya*.

### Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi
**Lord Curzon** split Bengal. It took effect on **16 October 1905**. The stated reason was easier administration. The real aim was to weaken Bengali nationalism.
- East: **East Bengal and Assam**, Muslim-majority.
- West: Bengal, Hindu-majority.

The reply was the **Swadeshi and Boycott movement**:
- boycott of foreign cloth and salt;
- **Raksha Bandhan** as a sign of unity (Tagore's idea); *Amar Sonar Bangla* as the marching song;
- national schools (**National Council of Education, 1906**) and volunteer groups (samitis).

The partition was **annulled in 1911** at the Delhi Durbar, under **Hardinge**. The capital was to shift from Calcutta to **Delhi**.

### Year by year, 1906 to 1916
| Year | Event | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| **1906** | **Muslim League** | Founded at **Dacca** (Nawab Salimullah). Backed the partition; soon asked for separate electorates. |
| 1906 | Calcutta session | President Naoroji; the word **Swaraj** first used in a Congress resolution |
| **1907** | **Surat split** | Moderates (president Rash Behari Ghosh) against Extremists (Tilak) |
| **1909** | **Morley–Minto Reforms** (Indian Councils Act) | **Separate electorates** for Muslims; Satyendra P. Sinha became the first Indian in the Viceroy's executive council. Minto: "father of communal electorates". |
| 1911 | Delhi Durbar | Partition annulled; capital to Delhi |
| **1916** | **Lucknow Pact** | Congress–League pact; Moderates and Extremists reunite; Congress accepted separate electorates |
| **1916** | **Home Rule Leagues** | **Tilak** (April, Belgaum; Maharashtra, Karnataka, Central Provinces, Berar) and **Annie Besant** (September, Madras; rest of India) |

Besant ran the papers *New India* and *Commonweal*. She became Congress president in 1917.

> **Tip:** 1905 split of Bengal → 1906 League → 1907 split of Congress → 1909 separate electorates.

### Early revolutionaries
- **Chapekar brothers**: Poona, 1897.
- **Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki**: Muzaffarpur, 1908.
- **India House, London**: Shyamji Krishna Varma.
- **Ghadar Party (1913)**: **Lala Har Dayal**, Sohan Singh Bhakna; headquarters **Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco**.
- **Komagata Maru** incident: 1914.

patterns.name: Founding of the Congress
patterns.howToSpot: "The first session of the INC was held at", founder, first president, number of delegates.
steps: Place and date: Bombay, 28 December 1885.
Organiser: A.O. Hume. First president: W.C. Bonnerjee.
Delegates: 72. Viceroy: Dufferin.
patterns.why: The same five facts cover every question on the founding.

example.q:
The first session of the Indian National Congress (1885) was presided over by:
(a) A.O. Hume (b) W.C. Bonnerjee (c) Dadabhai Naoroji (d) Surendranath Banerjea
steps: Hume organised it but did not preside; cut (a).
The first president was Bonnerjee.

patterns.name: Moderate leader ↔ work or title
patterns.howToSpot: "Drain of Wealth theory", "Grand Old Man of India", "Gandhi's political guru", "Lion of Bombay".
steps: Naoroji = drain theory, Grand Old Man, first Indian MP (1892).
Gokhale = Servants of India Society, Gandhi's guru.
Banerjea = Indian Association, *Bengalee*; Mehta = Lion of Bombay; R.C. Dutt = *Economic History of India*.
patterns.why: Each Moderate has one title or book that the question uses as the clue.

example.q: The Drain of Wealth theory was put forward by:
steps: Drain of wealth = India's money flowing out as salaries, pensions and profits.
It is in *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* (1901).

patterns.name: Extremist ↔ slogan, paper or festival
patterns.howToSpot: "Swaraj is my birthright", *Kesari*, Ganapati festival, Lal-Bal-Pal, Punjab Kesari.
steps: Tilak = *Kesari* + *Mahratta*, Ganapati 1893, Shivaji 1895, the Swaraj slogan.
Lajpat Rai = Punjab Kesari; Pal = Bengal; Aurobindo = *Bande Mataram*.
Check the language: *Kesari* Marathi, *Mahratta* English.
patterns.why: Tilak owns most of the clues, so first test whether the answer is Tilak.

example.q: The slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it" was given by:
steps: Swaraj slogan + Kesari editor = one leader.
He was jailed in Mandalay.

patterns.name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi
patterns.howToSpot: "Partition of Bengal was annulled in", which Viceroy, the two new provinces, Swadeshi methods.
steps: Curzon; effective 16 October 1905.
East Bengal and Assam (Muslim-majority) + West Bengal (Hindu-majority).
Reply: Swadeshi, boycott, Raksha Bandhan, National Council of Education 1906.
Annulled 1911 under Hardinge at the Delhi Durbar.
patterns.why: The partition story has a fixed start (Curzon 1905) and end (Hardinge 1911).

example.q: The partition of Bengal (1905) was annulled in:
steps: Curzon made it; Hardinge undid it.
The Delhi Durbar also announced the capital shift.

patterns.name: Surat split, Muslim League and Lucknow reunion
patterns.howToSpot: "The Congress split at Surat in", League's founding place, Congress–League pact.
steps: Surat 1907: Moderates (Rash Behari Ghosh) against Extremists (Tilak).
Muslim League 1906 at Dacca, Nawab Salimullah.
Lucknow 1916: reunion + Congress–League pact.
patterns.why: Split in 1907 and reunion in 1916 bracket this whole period.

example.q: The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at:
steps: 1906 League + Nawab Salimullah.
It was founded in East Bengal's main city.

patterns.name: Morley–Minto 1909 and Home Rule Leagues
patterns.howToSpot: "Separate electorates were introduced by", Home Rule Leagues — who, when, where.
steps: Morley–Minto 1909 = separate electorates; S.P. Sinha in the council.
Home Rule 1916: Tilak (April, Belgaum) and Besant (September, Madras).
Besant's papers: *New India*, *Commonweal*.
patterns.why: Both are linked to one year each: 1909 and 1916.

example.q: Annie Besant started her Home Rule League in 1916 at:
steps: Tilak started his first, in April, at Belgaum.
Besant followed in September.

patterns.name: Arrange events of 1885–1916
patterns.howToSpot: "Arrange in chronological order" with INC, partition, League, Surat, Morley–Minto, Lucknow.
steps: Write the year beside each item.
Check first and last items against the options.
patterns.why: Every event here has a different year, so sorting is exact.

example.q: Arrange in order: 1. Surat split 2. Morley–Minto Reforms 3. Partition of Bengal 4. Lucknow Pact
steps: Partition 1905, Surat 1907, Morley–Minto 1909, Lucknow 1916.

patterns.name: Early revolutionaries ↔ event
patterns.howToSpot: Khudiram Bose, Chapekar brothers, Ghadar Party, India House, Komagata Maru.
steps: Chapekar brothers = Poona, 1897.
Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki = Muzaffarpur, 1908.
Ghadar Party 1913 = Har Dayal, Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco.
India House, London = Shyamji Krishna Varma.
patterns.why: Each revolutionary group has one place, which is the usual clue.

example.q: The Ghadar Party (1913) had its headquarters at:
steps: Ghadar = Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna.
Headquarters: Yugantar Ashram in the USA.

revision: INC: 28 Dec 1885, Bombay, 72 delegates; Hume organised; Bonnerjee presided; Viceroy Dufferin.
Moderates: Naoroji (drain theory, first Indian MP 1892), Gokhale, S.N. Banerjea, Mehta, R.C. Dutt.
Extremists: Lal-Bal-Pal + Aurobindo; Tilak = Kesari, Mahratta, Mandalay, Gita Rahasya.
Curzon's partition effective 16 Oct 1905 → Swadeshi → annulled 1911.
1906 League (Dacca) and Swaraj at Calcutta; 1907 Surat split; 1909 Morley–Minto separate electorates.
1916: Lucknow Pact + Home Rule (Tilak April, Besant September).
Ghadar Party 1913: Har Dayal, San Francisco; Komagata Maru 1914.

subtopics.title: Gandhian Era & Road to Independence (1915–1947)
subtopics.concept: Gandhi returned to India in 1915 and led the freedom struggle through mass movements. Each movement has a year, a cause and an end. Exams mostly ask dates, places, session presidents and pacts, often as a chronological order question.

example.q: Gandhi's first hunger strike in India was during:
steps: Hunger strike = the "A" in C-A-K.
Ahmedabad 1918, for the mill workers' bonus.

tricks.title: Dandi numbers
tricks.body: **12 March** start · **6 April** salt law broken · **78** marchers · about **385 km** (240 miles) · from **Sabarmati Ashram**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Purna Swaraj was declared on 26 January 1930.
mistakes.right: It was **adopted at Lahore in December 1929**. 26 January 1930 was the first Independence Day.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the Poona Pact was between Gandhi and Irwin.
mistakes.right: Poona Pact (1932) = **Gandhi and Ambedkar**. Gandhi–Irwin Pact = 1931.

mistakes.wrong: Placing the Quit India launch in Delhi.
mistakes.right: Quit India was launched at **Gowalia Tank, Bombay**, on 8 August 1942.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the Azad Hind Government was set up in Rangoon or Tokyo.
mistakes.right: It was proclaimed in **Singapore** (21 October 1943).

mistakes.wrong: Calling Champaran Gandhi's first hunger strike.
mistakes.right: Champaran (1917) was his first **satyagraha** in India. The first **hunger strike** was at Ahmedabad (1918).

mistakes.wrong: Mixing the Communal Award and the Poona Pact.
mistakes.right: Communal Award gave **separate** electorates. Poona Pact replaced them with **reserved seats in joint** electorates.

subtopics.notes:
### Gandhi's first three struggles
Gandhi landed in India on **9 January 1915**, now **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**. He had built the method of **satyagraha** (truth-force, peaceful resistance) in South Africa from 1906.

| Year | Struggle | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| **1917** | **Champaran**, Bihar | Against forced indigo growing (**tinkathia** system). **Rajkumar Shukla** brought Gandhi. His **first satyagraha in India**. |
| 1918 | **Ahmedabad** mill strike | For workers' plague bonus. His **first hunger strike**. |
| 1918 | **Kheda**, Gujarat | **No-revenue** campaign for famine-hit farmers, with **Vallabhbhai Patel** |

### Rowlatt to Swaraj Party (1919 to 1923)
- **Rowlatt Act (1919):** arrest without trial — "no dalil, no vakil, no appeal". A nationwide hartal followed.
- **Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar (13 April 1919, Baisakhi):** **General Dyer** fired on an unarmed crowd. **Tagore** gave up his knighthood. The **Hunter Committee** enquired. **Udham Singh** shot Michael O'Dwyer in London (1940).
- **Khilafat movement** (Ali brothers): joined with Gandhi's **Non-Cooperation Movement (NCM)**. NCM began on **1 August 1920**. A Calcutta special session approved it; the Nagpur session ratified it. People boycotted schools, courts, titles and foreign cloth.
- **Chauri Chaura (5 February 1922, Gorakhpur):** a mob burnt a police station. Gandhi withdrew the NCM (Bardoli resolution).
- **Swaraj Party (1923):** **C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru**; they entered the councils.

### From Simon to Purna Swaraj
- **Simon Commission** (appointed 1927, arrived 1928): all-white, met with "**Simon Go Back**". **Lala Lajpat Rai** was hurt in a lathi charge at Lahore and died on 17 November 1928.
- **Nehru Report (1928)**, by Motilal Nehru: first Indian draft constitution; asked for Dominion Status.
- **Lahore session (December 1929)**: president **Jawaharlal Nehru**; **Purna Swaraj** (complete independence) resolution. **26 January 1930** was the first Independence Day.

### Civil Disobedience (1930–34)
Gandhi's **Dandi March** broke the salt law.
- Started **12 March 1930** from **Sabarmati Ashram** with **78** followers.
- About **385 km** (240 miles); salt law broken at Dandi on **6 April 1930**.

| Year | Event | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| 1931 | **Gandhi–Irwin Pact** (5 March) | Ended this phase; Gandhi went alone to the **Second Round Table Conference** |
| 1931 | **Karachi session** | President **Vallabhbhai Patel**; resolution on **Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy** |
| 1932 | **Communal Award** | Separate electorates for the Depressed Classes |
| 1932 | **Poona Pact** (24 Sept) | **Gandhi and Ambedkar**: reserved seats instead, within joint electorates |
| 1935 | **Government of India Act** | Provincial autonomy; basis of much of the Constitution; Congress ministries 1937–39 |

### Quit India and the INA (1939–1945)
- **1939, Tripuri:** Subhas Bose was re-elected president, then resigned and formed the **Forward Bloc**.
- **1940:** August Offer; **Individual Satyagraha** — **Vinoba Bhave** was the first satyagrahi.
- **March 1942:** **Cripps Mission** — Gandhi called it a "post-dated cheque on a crashing bank".
- **8 August 1942:** **Quit India** resolution at **Gowalia Tank, Bombay**; slogan **"Do or Die"**. Leaders were arrested at once. **Aruna Asaf Ali** hoisted the flag. **Usha Mehta** ran the Congress Radio. Parallel governments came up at **Ballia** (Chittu Pandey), **Satara** (Nana Patil) and **Tamluk**.
- **21 October 1943:** **Subhas Bose** proclaimed the **Azad Hind Government** in **Singapore**. INA slogan: "**Delhi Chalo**". He also said "Give me blood, I will give you freedom". The **Rani Jhansi Regiment** was led by Lakshmi Sahgal.

### Road to freedom (1946–47)
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 1946 | RIN (navy) mutiny; **Cabinet Mission** — Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps, Alexander |
| 16 Aug 1946 | **Direct Action Day** |
| 2 Sept 1946 | Interim Government formed |
| 3 June 1947 | **Mountbatten Plan** |
| 18 July 1947 | Indian Independence Act |
| **15 Aug 1947** | Independence |

### Revolutionaries of the 1920s and 1930s
| Event | Date | People |
|---|---|---|
| **Kakori train action** | 9 Aug 1925 | **Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan** (HRA) |
| HSRA formed | 1928 | Bhagat Singh, **Chandrashekhar Azad** (Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi) |
| Central Assembly bomb | **8 April 1929** | **Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt** |
| Chittagong armoury raid | 1930 | **Surya Sen** |
| Hanged | **23 March 1931** | Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev (Martyrs' Day) |

> **Tip:** Session presidents: **Lahore 1929 = Jawaharlal**, **Karachi 1931 = Patel**, **Tripuri 1939 = Bose**.

patterns.name: Gandhi's early satyagrahas
patterns.howToSpot: "Gandhi's first satyagraha in India", tinkathia, first hunger strike, no-revenue campaign.
steps: Champaran 1917 = indigo, tinkathia, Bihar, first satyagraha.
Ahmedabad 1918 = mill workers, first hunger strike.
Kheda 1918 = no revenue, with Patel.
patterns.why: The three struggles differ in one word each: indigo, mill, revenue.

example.q:
In which struggle did Gandhi first use a hunger strike in India?
(a) Champaran (b) Kheda (c) Ahmedabad mill strike (d) Bardoli
steps: Champaran = first satyagraha, not hunger strike; cut (a).
Kheda = no-revenue; Bardoli (1928) was Patel's movement.

patterns.name: Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh
patterns.howToSpot: "No dalil, no vakil, no appeal", Jallianwala date, General Dyer, reactions.
steps: Rowlatt Act 1919 = arrest without trial.
Jallianwala: 13 April 1919, Baisakhi, Amritsar, General Dyer.
Reactions: Tagore gave up his knighthood; Hunter Committee; Udham Singh shot O'Dwyer (1940).
patterns.why: The Rowlatt Act led straight to the Amritsar meeting, so the facts come as a set.

example.q: Who gave up his knighthood in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
steps: Massacre: 13 April 1919.
The poet who returned his title was Tagore.

patterns.name: Non-Cooperation and Chauri Chaura
patterns.howToSpot: "Why was the NCM withdrawn?", Chauri Chaura, Khilafat, Swaraj Party.
steps: NCM began 1 August 1920, joined with Khilafat.
Chauri Chaura, 5 February 1922: police station burnt, NCM withdrawn.
Swaraj Party 1923: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.
patterns.why: Violence at Chauri Chaura broke Gandhi's non-violence rule, so he stopped the movement.

example.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn in 1922 after the incident at:
steps: 1922 + violence + police station.
The place was in Gorakhpur district.

patterns.name: Dandi March and the pacts
patterns.howToSpot: Dandi dates, salt law, Gandhi–Irwin Pact, Round Table Conference, Communal Award, Poona Pact.
steps: Dandi: 12 March–6 April 1930, 78 marchers, from Sabarmati.
Gandhi–Irwin Pact: 5 March 1931; then Second Round Table Conference.
Communal Award 1932 → Poona Pact 1932 (Gandhi and Ambedkar).
patterns.why: One pact per year: 1931 with Irwin, 1932 with Ambedkar.

example.q:
The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between Gandhi and:
(a) Lord Irwin (b) B.R. Ambedkar (c) Jinnah (d) Subhas Bose
steps: Irwin is the 1931 pact; cut (a).
The Poona Pact settled seats for the Depressed Classes.

patterns.name: Simon Commission to Purna Swaraj
patterns.howToSpot: Simon Commission, Lajpat Rai's death, Nehru Report, Lahore 1929, 26 January 1930.
steps: Simon: appointed 1927, arrived 1928, all-white, "Simon Go Back".
Lajpat Rai hurt at Lahore; died 17 November 1928.
Nehru Report 1928 (Motilal); Lahore December 1929 (Jawaharlal), Purna Swaraj.
patterns.why: Each step answered the previous one, so the order is fixed.

example.q: The Purna Swaraj resolution was passed at the Lahore session under the presidency of:
steps: Lahore, December 1929.
Session presidents: Lahore = Jawaharlal.

patterns.name: Quit India, INA and the last steps
patterns.howToSpot: "Do or Die", Gowalia Tank, parallel governments, Azad Hind, Cabinet Mission, Mountbatten Plan.
steps: Quit India: 8 August 1942, Gowalia Tank, Bombay, "Do or Die".
Heroes: Aruna Asaf Ali (flag), Usha Mehta (radio); Ballia, Satara, Tamluk.
Bose: Azad Hind, Singapore, 21 October 1943.
Cabinet Mission 1946 → Mountbatten Plan 3 June 1947 → 15 August 1947.
patterns.why: The last five years have many firsts, but each name has one clear role.

example.q: Aruna Asaf Ali is remembered in the Quit India Movement for:
steps: Leaders were arrested the night of 8 August 1942.
She raised the flag at Gowalia Tank, Bombay.
example.answer: Hoisting the flag at Gowalia Tank

patterns.name: Arrange freedom-movement events in order
patterns.howToSpot: "Arrange in chronological order" with any four events from 1915 to 1947.
steps: Write the year (and month if two share a year) beside each item.
Find the earliest; keep only options that start with it.
Check the last item to pick between the rest.
patterns.why: This is the most asked question type in the topic, and years settle it.

example.q: Arrange in order: 1. Dandi March 2. Chauri Chaura 3. Quit India 4. Jallianwala Bagh
steps: Jallianwala 1919, Chauri Chaura 1922, Dandi 1930, Quit India 1942.

patterns.name: Revolutionary ↔ action
patterns.howToSpot: Kakori, Assembly bomb, Chittagong raid, HSRA, Bhagat Singh's execution.
steps: Kakori 1925 = Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan.
HSRA 1928 = Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad.
Assembly bomb 8 April 1929 = Bhagat Singh, B.K. Dutt; Chittagong 1930 = Surya Sen.
23 March 1931 = Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev hanged.
patterns.why: Each action has one or two names, so match the event first.

example.q: Who threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929 along with Bhagat Singh?
steps: Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged with him but did not throw the bomb.
His partner in the Assembly was B.K. Dutt.

revision: Return 9 Jan 1915 → Champaran 1917 → Ahmedabad and Kheda 1918.
1919: Rowlatt Act → Jallianwala (13 April, Dyer) → Tagore gives up knighthood.
NCM 1 Aug 1920 → Chauri Chaura 5 Feb 1922 → Swaraj Party 1923.
Simon 1928 → Nehru Report 1928 → Lahore 1929 (Purna Swaraj) → 26 Jan 1930.
Dandi 12 March–6 April 1930 → Gandhi–Irwin 5 March 1931 → Poona Pact 24 Sept 1932.
Quit India 8 Aug 1942, Gowalia Tank, "Do or Die"; Azad Hind, Singapore, 21 Oct 1943.
Mountbatten Plan 3 June 1947 → Independence Act 18 July → 15 Aug 1947.
Bhagat Singh: Assembly bomb 8 April 1929; hanged 23 March 1931.

subtopics.title: Newspapers, Journals & Books of the Freedom Era
subtopics.concept: Newspapers and books spread the ideas of the freedom movement across India. Most questions name a paper or a book and ask who started or wrote it. Learn each one as a pair: paper with editor, book with author.

tricks.title: Gandhi's papers: "YNH"
tricks.body: **Y**oung India · **N**avajivan · **H**arijan (plus *Indian Opinion* from South Africa). Any other paper in the options belongs to someone else.

example.q: Which of these was NOT edited by Gandhi: Young India, Harijan, Kesari, Navajivan?
steps: Y-N-H covers Young India, Navajivan and Harijan.
Kesari is left over; it was Tilak's Marathi paper.

tricks.title: Books written in jail
tricks.body: Tilak → *Gita Rahasya* in **Mandalay**. Nehru → *The Discovery of India* in **Ahmednagar Fort**.

mistakes.wrong: Giving *Al-Hilal* to Mohammad Ali.
mistakes.right: *Al-Hilal* = **Abul Kalam Azad**. *Comrade* = **Mohammad Ali Jauhar**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying *Anandamath* was written by Tagore.
mistakes.right: *Anandamath* is by **Bankim Chandra**. *Jana Gana Mana* and *Amar Sonar Bangla* are by **Tagore**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Ripon passed the Vernacular Press Act.
mistakes.right: **Lytton** passed it (1878). **Ripon** repealed it (1882).

mistakes.wrong: Giving *New India* to Bipin Chandra Pal or Nehru.
mistakes.right: *New India* was **Annie Besant's** paper, with *Commonweal*.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing Naoroji's and R.C. Dutt's books.
mistakes.right: Naoroji = *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*. Dutt = *Economic History of India*.

subtopics.notes:
### Why the press mattered
The national movement ran on print. Newspapers built all-India opinion and spread calls for boycott. Their editors often faced cases and jail.

Learn three things for each paper: its editor, its language and its year.

> **Example:** *Kesari* → Tilak → Marathi. *Mahratta* → Tilak → English.

### The first papers and press laws
- ***Bengal Gazette* (1780)**: **James Augustus Hicky**. The first newspaper in India, in English.
- **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**: *Sambad Kaumudi* (Bengali, 1821) and *Mirat-ul-Akbar* (Persian, 1822).
- **Metcalfe (1835)** was called the "liberator of the Indian press".
- ***Amrita Bazar Patrika* (1868)**: the Ghosh brothers, Sisir Kumar and Motilal. It began in Bengali.
- ***The Hindu* (1878, Madras)**: **G. Subramania Iyer**.
- **Vernacular Press Act (1878)**: Lytton's "Gagging Act". It gagged Indian-language papers. *Amrita Bazar Patrika* became an English paper **overnight** to escape it. **Ripon** repealed the Act in **1882**.

### Papers of the freedom struggle
| Paper | Language | Person |
|---|---|---|
| *Bengalee* | English | Surendranath Banerjea |
| *Kesari* / *Mahratta* (1881) | Marathi / English | **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** |
| *Indian Opinion* (1903) | English, Gujarati and others | Gandhi (South Africa) |
| *Young India* / *Navajivan* | English / Gujarati | **Gandhi**, in the Non-Cooperation years |
| ***Harijan*** (1933) | English weekly | **Gandhi**, against untouchability |
| ***Al-Hilal*** (1912), *Al-Balagh* | Urdu | **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** |
| *Comrade* | English | Mohammad Ali Jauhar (one of the Ali brothers) |
| *Bande Mataram* | English | **Aurobindo Ghosh**, with Bipin Chandra Pal |
| *New India*, *Commonweal* | English | **Annie Besant** |
| *Mooknayak* (1920) | Marathi | **B.R. Ambedkar** |
| *National Herald* (1938) | English | Jawaharlal Nehru |
| *Tahdhib-ul-Akhlaq* | — | Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (Aligarh message) |

*Harijan* also had sister papers: *Harijan Bandhu* (Gujarati) and *Harijan Sevak* (Hindi).

> **Tip:** Gandhi's papers are **Y-N-H**: *Young India*, *Navajivan*, *Harijan* (plus *Indian Opinion* in South Africa).

### Books and their authors
| Book | Author |
|---|---|
| *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* (1901) | **Dadabhai Naoroji** (drain theory) |
| *Economic History of India* | R.C. Dutt |
| *Anandamath* (1882) | **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay** |
| *Gita Rahasya* | Tilak, written in **Mandalay** jail |
| ***Hind Swaraj*** (1909) | **Gandhi** |
| *My Experiments with Truth* (autobiography, 1927) | Gandhi |
| *Gulamgiri* (1873) | Jyotirao Phule |
| *Annihilation of Caste* (1936) | B.R. Ambedkar |
| *The Indian Struggle* (1935) | Subhas Chandra Bose |
| *Glimpses of World History* (1934) | Jawaharlal Nehru |
| *Toward Freedom* (autobiography, 1936) | Jawaharlal Nehru |
| *The Discovery of India* (1946) | Jawaharlal Nehru, written in **Ahmednagar Fort** jail |
| *India Wins Freedom* | Maulana Abul Kalam Azad |
| *India Divided* | Rajendra Prasad |
| *Unhappy India* (1928) | Lala Lajpat Rai; a reply to Katherine Mayo's *Mother India* |
| *Why I Am an Atheist* | Bhagat Singh |
| *Neel Darpan* (play) | Dinabandhu Mitra |

> **Rule:** Nehru has three books to know: *Glimpses* (1934), *Toward Freedom* (1936), *Discovery* (1946).

### Songs that came from print
- **Vande Mataram** comes from Bankim Chandra's novel ***Anandamath*** (1882). **Tagore** first sang it at the **1896 Calcutta Congress session**.
- **Tagore** wrote ***Amar Sonar Bangla*** during the 1905 Swadeshi movement. It later became Bangladesh's national anthem.
- *Jana Gana Mana* is also by **Tagore**, not Bankim.

patterns.name: Newspaper ↔ editor or founder
patterns.howToSpot: "Who edited Kesari?", "New India was published by", or a match-the-column of papers and editors.
steps: Recall the big four: Tilak (Kesari, Mahratta), Gandhi (Young India, Navajivan, Harijan), Besant (New India, Commonweal), Azad (Al-Hilal).
Then the rest: Banerjea (Bengalee), Mohammad Ali (Comrade), Aurobindo (Bande Mataram), Ambedkar (Mooknayak).
Match the sure pairs first and cut options.
patterns.why: Each paper has one main editor, so one sure pair clears most options.

example.q:
The newspaper *New India*, which carried the Home Rule campaign, was started by:
(a) Bipin Chandra Pal (b) Annie Besant (c) Jawaharlal Nehru (d) Tilak
steps: Home Rule + *New India* point to the September 1916 League leader.
Nehru's paper was *National Herald*; Tilak's was *Kesari*.

patterns.name: Book ↔ author
patterns.howToSpot: "Who wrote The Discovery of India?", "Gulamgiri is a work of", or a book–author match.
steps: Gandhi: Hind Swaraj, My Experiments with Truth.
Nehru: Glimpses, Toward Freedom, Discovery of India.
Naoroji vs R.C. Dutt: Poverty and Un-British Rule vs Economic History.
Azad: India Wins Freedom; Prasad: India Divided; Bose: The Indian Struggle; Ambedkar: Annihilation of Caste.
patterns.why: Most book questions draw from this short list of leaders.

example.q: The book *The Discovery of India* was written by:
steps: It was written in Ahmednagar Fort jail and published in 1946.
It is one of Nehru's three books.

patterns.name: Press laws
patterns.howToSpot: "Vernacular Press Act was passed/repealed by", "liberator of the Indian press", paper that changed language overnight.
steps: Vernacular Press Act 1878 = Lytton.
Repealed 1882 = Ripon.
Metcalfe 1835 = liberator of the press.
Amrita Bazar Patrika became English overnight.
patterns.why: Only three names and one paper appear in press-law questions.

example.q: The Vernacular Press Act (1878) was repealed by:
steps: Lytton passed it in 1878.
Ripon, the next reformer Viceroy, repealed it in 1882.

patterns.name: Gandhi's journals
patterns.howToSpot: "Harijan was started in", paper of the Non-Cooperation years, language of Navajivan.
steps: South Africa: Indian Opinion (1903).
Non-Cooperation: Young India (English), Navajivan (Gujarati).
Harijan (1933): English weekly; Harijan Bandhu (Gujarati), Harijan Sevak (Hindi).
patterns.why: Gandhi's papers change with his phase of work, so the year points to the paper.

example.q: Gandhi started the English weekly *Harijan* in:
steps: *Harijan* was for the campaign against untouchability.
It came after Civil Disobedience began.

patterns.name: Anandamath, Vande Mataram and protest writing
patterns.howToSpot: Source of Vande Mataram, where it was first sung, Amar Sonar Bangla, Unhappy India.
steps: Vande Mataram: from Anandamath (1882), Bankim Chandra.
First sung by Tagore at the 1896 Calcutta Congress.
Amar Sonar Bangla: Tagore, 1905; later Bangladesh's anthem.
Unhappy India (1928): Lajpat Rai's reply to *Mother India*.
patterns.why: Song questions test the book, the writer and the first singing together.

example.q: The song Vande Mataram first appeared in:
steps: The song is by Bankim Chandra.
It is part of his 1882 novel.

patterns.name: Odd one out: not by this person
patterns.howToSpot: "Which of these was NOT edited/written by X?"
steps: List X's papers or books from memory.
Tick every option that is on the list.
The option left over is the answer; check who it really belongs to.
patterns.why: Knowing a person's full list is faster than checking each option alone.

example.q:
Which of these books was NOT written by Jawaharlal Nehru?
(a) Glimpses of World History (b) Toward Freedom (c) India Wins Freedom (d) The Discovery of India
steps: Nehru's three: Glimpses, Toward Freedom, Discovery.
*India Wins Freedom* is by Maulana Azad.

patterns.name: Language of a paper
patterns.howToSpot: "Kesari was published in which language?" or "Al-Hilal was an ___ weekly".
steps: Marathi: Kesari, Mooknayak. English: Mahratta, Young India, New India, Bengalee.
Gujarati: Navajivan. Urdu: Al-Hilal. Bengali: Sambad Kaumudi. Persian: Mirat-ul-Akbar.
Watch pairs by one editor that use two languages.
patterns.why: Some editors ran two papers in two languages, which is the usual trap.

example.q: *Mirat-ul-Akbar*, started by Ram Mohan Roy in 1822, was published in:
steps: Roy had two papers.
Sambad Kaumudi was Bengali; Mirat-ul-Akbar was the other one.

revision: First newspaper: Bengal Gazette (1780), James Augustus Hicky.
Roy: Sambad Kaumudi (Bengali) + Mirat-ul-Akbar (Persian).
Vernacular Press Act 1878 (Lytton) → repealed 1882 (Ripon); Amrita Bazar Patrika turned English overnight.
Tilak: Kesari + Mahratta; Besant: New India + Commonweal; Azad: Al-Hilal; Ambedkar: Mooknayak.
Gandhi: Indian Opinion, Young India, Navajivan, Harijan (1933); Hind Swaraj (1909).
Nehru: Glimpses 1934, Toward Freedom 1936, Discovery of India 1946.
Vande Mataram from Anandamath (1882), first sung by Tagore at Calcutta, 1896.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Arrange 3-4 events in order, or "which happened first?"
pyqPatterns.approach:
Learn anchor years: 1757, 1857, 1885, 1905, 1919, 1930, 1942, 1947.
Place each event near an anchor year.

example.q: Arrange: (1) Jallianwala Bagh (2) Chauri Chaura (3) Dandi March (4) Quit India.
example.solution:
Jallianwala Bagh: 1919
Chauri Chaura: 1922
Dandi March: 1930, Quit India: 1942
The order is **1, 2, 3, 4**

pyqPatterns.pattern: Governor-General or Viceroy and his work
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "Who was Governor-General when...?" or "the Doctrine of Lapse was used by..."
pyqPatterns.approach:
Bentinck = ended sati. Dalhousie = Doctrine of Lapse and railways.
Lytton = Vernacular Press Act. Ripon = local self-government. Curzon = partition of Bengal.

example.q: Under which Governor-General was the Doctrine of Lapse used to annex states?
example.solution:
Under the Doctrine of Lapse, a state without a natural heir was annexed
It was used between 1848 and 1856
The Governor-General then was Dalhousie
**Dalhousie**

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A city (Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi) is named, and its leader is asked.
pyqPatterns.approach:
Learn the pairs.
Delhi = Bahadur Shah II, Kanpur = Nana Saheb, Lucknow = Begum Hazrat Mahal, Jhansi = Rani Lakshmibai.

example.q: Who led the 1857 revolt at Kanpur?
example.solution:
Kanpur's leader was the adopted son of Baji Rao II
Tantia Tope was his commander
Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal instead
**Nana Saheb**

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "The Lahore session of 1929 was led by..." or "where was Purna Swaraj declared?"
pyqPatterns.approach:
1885 Bombay = W.C. Bonnerjee. 1906 Calcutta = Naoroji (Swaraj). 1907 Surat = split.
1929 Lahore = Nehru (Purna Swaraj).

example.q: Who presided over the 1929 Lahore session that declared Purna Swaraj?
example.solution:
The Lahore session was held in 1929
It demanded complete independence (Purna Swaraj)
The president was Jawaharlal Nehru
**Jawaharlal Nehru**

pyqPatterns.pattern: Newspaper or book and its writer
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "Kesari was edited by..." or "who wrote The Discovery of India?"
pyqPatterns.approach:
Tilak = Kesari and Mahratta. Gandhi = Young India, Navajivan, Harijan, Hind Swaraj.
Nehru = Discovery of India, Glimpses of World History.

example.q: Who wrote India Wins Freedom?
example.solution:
India Wins Freedom is an autobiography
It was written by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
Rajendra Prasad wrote India Divided (do not mix them)
**Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Statements about a movement are given, and the correct ones are picked.
pyqPatterns.approach:
For each movement note four things: what started it, its main method, where it spread, how it ended.
Civil Disobedience: salt march to Dandi, ended (paused) by the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

example.q: How did the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930 begin?
example.solution:
Gandhi marched from Sabarmati on 12 March 1930
He reached Dandi on the coast
On 6 April he broke the salt law
**By breaking the salt law at Dandi**

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "Swaraj is my birthright" or "Give me blood" — who said it?
pyqPatterns.approach:
Tilak = "Swaraj is my birthright". Gandhi = "Do or Die".
Bose = "Give me blood" and "Dilli Chalo". Nehru = "Tryst with Destiny".

example.q: Who said "Give me blood, I will give you freedom"?
example.solution:
The words were said to the Indian National Army
The leader of the INA was Netaji
He also gave the call "Dilli Chalo"
**Subhas Chandra Bose**

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "The Brahmo Samaj was founded by..." or "sati was abolished in..."
pyqPatterns.approach:
Ram Mohan Roy = Brahmo Sabha (1828). Dayananda = Arya Samaj (1875).
Vivekananda = Ramakrishna Mission (1897). Syed Ahmad Khan = Aligarh (MAO College).

example.q: Whose campaign led to the legal ban on sati in 1829?
example.solution:
Sati was banned in 1829
The law was passed by Governor-General Bentinck
The campaign behind it was led by Raja Ram Mohan Roy
**Raja Ram Mohan Roy**

solvedExamples.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Rowlatt Satyagraha
2. Arrival of the Simon Commission
3. Champaran Satyagraha
4. Gandhi–Irwin Pact
solvedExamples.solution: Champaran **1917** → Rowlatt Satyagraha **1919** → Simon Commission **1928** → Gandhi–Irwin Pact **1931**. Order: 3, 1, 2, 4.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Champaran is Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, so it must come first → only A and C remain; Rowlatt (1919) is before Simon (1928) → A.

solvedExamples.q: Which of the following pairs of Governor-General/Viceroy and measure is **NOT** correctly matched?
options: Lord Canning — First Viceroy of India
solvedExamples.solution: The **Ilbert Bill (1883)**, which allowed Indian judges to try Europeans, came under **Lord Ripon**. Curzon is linked with the partition of Bengal (1905). The other three pairs are correct.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Ripon is the 'liberal' Viceroy — both the local self-government resolution and the Ilbert Bill belong to him.

solvedExamples.q: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the Revolt of 1857 at —
solvedExamples.solution: **Begum Hazrat Mahal** of Awadh led the rising at **Lucknow** and proclaimed her son Birjis Qadr ruler. Kanpur – Nana Saheb; Jhansi – Rani Lakshmibai; Faizabad – Maulvi Ahmadullah.

solvedExamples.q: The resolution on **Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy** was adopted by the Indian National Congress at its 1931 session held at —
solvedExamples.solution: The **Karachi session (March 1931)**, presided over by **Vallabhbhai Patel**, adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme and endorsed the Gandhi–Irwin Pact. Lahore (1929) adopted Purna Swaraj.

practice.q: The **Battle of Plassey**, in which Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, was fought in —
practice.solution: Plassey was fought on **23 June 1757**. 1764 = Buxar; 1761 = Third Panipat; 1799 = death of Tipu Sultan.

practice.q: The **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa was granted to the East India Company by the —
practice.solution: After Buxar, Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani (right to collect revenue) through the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)**. Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War; Srirangapatna (1792) the Third Anglo-Mysore War.

practice.q: The **Subsidiary Alliance** system was introduced by —
practice.solution: **Lord Wellesley** (1798–1805) made Indian rulers keep British troops at their own cost and accept a British Resident; the Nizam of Hyderabad signed first (1798).

practice.q: The **Permanent Settlement** of land revenue in Bengal (1793) was introduced by —
practice.solution: **Lord Cornwallis** fixed revenue permanently with the zamindars in 1793. It is also called the Zamindari system.

practice.q: The practice of **sati** was declared illegal in 1829 during the tenure of —
practice.solution: The **Bengal Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII) of 1829** was passed by **Lord William Bentinck**, supported by the campaign of Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

practice.q: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at **Kanpur**?
practice.solution: **Nana Saheb**, adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II, led the revolt at Kanpur with Tantia Tope. Kunwar Singh – Jagdishpur (Bihar); Begum Hazrat Mahal – Lucknow; Khan Bahadur Khan – Bareilly.

practice.q: The **Arya Samaj** was founded in 1875 by —
practice.solution: **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** founded the Arya Samaj in **Bombay (1875)**. He wrote *Satyarth Prakash* and gave the call 'Back to the Vedas'.

practice.q: The **Satyashodhak Samaj** (1873), which worked for the rights of the lower castes, was founded by —
practice.solution: **Jyotirao Phule** founded the Satyashodhak Samaj ('Society of Truth-seekers') in 1873 in Maharashtra and wrote *Gulamgiri* the same year.
practice.shortcut: **P**hule = **P**eople of the lower castes; year **1873** = Gulamgiri year.

practice.q: The **Partition of Bengal** (1905) was carried out by which Viceroy?
practice.solution: **Lord Curzon** announced the partition, which took effect on **16 October 1905** and triggered the Swadeshi movement. It was annulled in **1911** under Lord Hardinge.

practice.q: The Indian National Congress split into Moderates and Extremists at its session held at **Surat** in —
practice.solution: The **Surat split** took place in **December 1907**. The two groups reunited at Lucknow in **1916**.
practice.shortcut: 5-6-**7**-9: Bengal split, League, **Congress split**, separate electorates.

practice.q: The **Champaran Satyagraha** (1917), Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, took place in present-day —
practice.solution: Champaran is in **Bihar**. Gandhi went there on Raj Kumar Shukla's request to take up the grievances of indigo cultivators under the **tinkathia** system.
practice.shortcut: **C**hamparan = first letter of the chain C-A-K; indigo in Bihar.

practice.q: Who renounced his knighthood in protest against the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** of 1919?
practice.solution: **Rabindranath Tagore** gave up the knighthood conferred on him in 1915 by writing to the Viceroy (Lord Chelmsford) in May 1919. Gandhi later returned his Kaiser-i-Hind medal.
practice.shortcut: Only a 'Sir' could renounce a knighthood → Sir Rabindranath.

practice.q: The **Purna Swaraj** resolution was adopted at the Lahore session of the Congress (1929) presided over by —
practice.solution: **Jawaharlal Nehru** presided over the **Lahore session (December 1929)**, which declared complete independence as the goal; 26 January 1930 was celebrated as Independence Day.

practice.q: Gandhi began the **Dandi March** from Sabarmati Ashram on —
practice.solution: The march started on **12 March 1930** and reached Dandi, where Gandhi broke the salt law on **6 April 1930**. 5 March 1931 is the Gandhi–Irwin Pact.
practice.shortcut: **12** March start, **6** April finish — start is always the March date.

practice.q: The **Poona Pact (1932)** on the representation of the depressed classes was signed between —
practice.solution: After the **Communal Award** (1932), Gandhi fasted in Yerawada jail. The **Poona Pact** with **B.R. Ambedkar** replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.

practice.q: The slogan **'Do or Die'** was given by Gandhi during the —
practice.solution: Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' on **8 August 1942** at **Gowalia Tank, Bombay**, when the Quit India resolution was passed.
practice.shortcut: 1942 = last big push → last-chance slogan 'Do or Die'.

practice.q: The headquarters of the **Ghadar Party** (Yugantar Ashram) was located in —
practice.solution: The Ghadar Party (1913), led by **Lala Har Dayal** and **Sohan Singh Bhakna**, was run from **Yugantar Ashram in San Francisco**, USA, and published the weekly *Ghadar*.
practice.shortcut: Ghadar = Indians on the **US Pacific coast** → San Francisco.

practice.q: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the **Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)** on 21 October 1943 at —
practice.solution: The Azad Hind Government was proclaimed in **Singapore**. The INA's HQ later moved to Rangoon; Bose had earlier worked from Berlin.

practice.q: The Urdu weekly ***Al-Hilal*** (1912) was started by —
practice.solution: **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** launched *Al-Hilal* from Calcutta in 1912. Mohammad Ali Jauhar edited *Comrade*.

practice.q: The **Battle of Buxar** was fought in —
practice.solution: **Buxar, 1764**: the Company's army under Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II.

practice.q: The first **Governor-General of Bengal** (under the Regulating Act, 1773) was —
practice.solution: **Warren Hastings** became Governor-General of Bengal in 1773; the title 'Governor-General of India' began with William Bentinck (1833).
practice.shortcut: Hastings first GG; Bentinck first 'of India'.

practice.q: Tipu Sultan is called the **'Tiger of Mysore'**. He was killed in —
practice.solution: Tipu died defending his capital **Srirangapatna** in the **Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799)** under Lord Wellesley.

practice.q: Under the **Doctrine of Lapse**, whose adoption claim as heir was rejected, leading to annexation?
practice.solution: **Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse** refused recognition to adopted heirs — Jhansi (Lakshmibai), Satara, Nagpur and others lapsed. Nana Saheb's pension claim was refused too.

practice.q: **English** was made the medium of higher education in India (Macaulay's Minute, 1835) under —
practice.solution: **Bentinck** accepted **Macaulay's Minute (1835)**, making English the medium of higher education; he also abolished sati (1829).

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878.
2. The Delhi Durbar of 1877 proclaimed Victoria 'Empress of India'.
3. The Arms Act of Lytton's time disarmed Indians.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three belong to **Lytton's** tenure (1876–80): the press gag (1878), the 1877 Durbar, and the Arms Act.
practice.shortcut: Lytton's trio: press gag, Arms Act, Durbar.

practice.q: In the **Mahalwari** system, the unit of settlement was —
practice.solution: **Mahalwari** settlement was made with the **village estate** as a whole (North-Western Provinces, Central India, parts of Punjab), following Holt Mackenzie's 1822 rules.

practice.q:
Match:
1. Permanent Settlement — Cornwallis
2. Ryotwari — Thomas Munro
3. Mahalwari — Lord Wellesley
Which pairs are correct?
practice.solution: **Cornwallis** (Permanent Settlement) and **Munro** (Ryotwari) are right; **Mahalwari** is associated with **Holt Mackenzie**, not Wellesley.
practice.shortcut: Wellesley belongs to Subsidiary Alliance — a classic distractor.

practice.q: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at **Jhansi**?
practice.solution: **Rani Lakshmibai** fought for Jhansi (her adopted heir was refused under the Doctrine of Lapse) and died at Gwalior in June 1858.

practice.q: **Kunwar Singh**, the aged leader of the 1857 revolt, was associated with —
practice.solution: **Kunwar Singh** of Jagdishpur, near Arrah in Bihar, fought the British through 1857-58.

practice.q:
Match:
1. Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan
2. Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah
3. Gwalior — Bakht Khan
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Bareilly-**Khan Bahadur Khan** and Faizabad-**Ahmadullah Shah** are right; **Bakht Khan** was the rebel general at **Delhi**, not Gwalior.
practice.shortcut: Gwalior belongs to the Rani; Bakht Khan to Delhi.

practice.q: The **immediate cause** of the Revolt of 1857 was —
practice.solution: The new **Enfield rifle cartridges**, rumoured greased with cow and pig fat, sparked the revolt — the deeper causes were political, economic and military.

practice.q: **Mangal Pandey** belonged to which regiment?
practice.solution: Mangal Pandey of the **34th Native Infantry** attacked officers at **Barrackpore** on 29 March 1857; the regiment was disbanded.

practice.q: The annexation of **Awadh in 1856** was justified by the British on the ground of —
practice.solution: **Awadh** was annexed in **1856** on grounds of 'misgovernment' — not Lapse. The annexation alienated the talukdars and sepoys (many were from Awadh).
practice.shortcut: Lapse for adopted heirs; Awadh = misgovernment.

practice.q: The Revolt of 1857 **broke out in full** at Meerut on —
practice.solution: On **10 May 1857** the Meerut sepoys mutinied and marched to Delhi, proclaiming Bahadur Shah II. (29 March = Barrackpore/Mangal Pandey.)

practice.q: After the fall of Delhi (1857), **Bahadur Shah II** was —
practice.solution: The old emperor was tried at Delhi and **exiled to Rangoon**, where he died in 1862; his sons were shot by Captain Hodson.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The Act of 1858 created the office of Secretary of State for India.
2. Canning became the first Viceroy.
3. The Queen's Proclamation was issued at Allahabad.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three are standard outcomes of 1858: the Secretary of State (with a 15-member Council), **Canning** as first Viceroy, and the **Proclamation at Allahabad** (1 November 1858).
practice.shortcut: The 1858 package: SoS + Viceroy + Allahabad Proclamation.

practice.q: The **Paika rebellion (1817)** of Odisha was led by —
practice.solution: **Bakshi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar**, the Paika (soldier-landholder) chief of Khurda, led the 1817 rebellion against British land and revenue changes.

practice.q: **Birsa Munda's** Ulgulan (1899-1900) was aimed at —
options: Driving out the British and outsiders from tribal land
practice.solution: The **Ulgulan** ('Great Tumult') of the Munda tribes demanded self-rule of tribal lands; its aftermath included the **Chotanagpur Tenancy Act (1908)**.

practice.q: Which pair of uprising and leader is **incorrectly** matched?
practice.solution: The **Moplahs are Muslim peasants of Malabar**, not Paikas (the Paikas are Odisha's soldier-landholders of the 1817 rebellion). The other three pairs are correct.

practice.q: The **Brahmo Samaj** was founded in 1828 by —
practice.solution: **Ram Mohan Roy** founded the Brahmo Sabha (later Samaj) in **1828** — preaching monotheism and against idol worship.

practice.q: The **Ramakrishna Mission** was founded in 1897 by —
practice.solution: **Vivekananda** founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897) in his guru Ramakrishna's name — its motto: service to man as service to God.

practice.q: The **Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College** of 1875, which became Aligarh Muslim University, was founded by —
practice.solution: **Sir Syed Ahmed Khan** founded MAO College (1875) — the heart of the Aligarh movement for modern education among Muslims.

practice.q: Who opened one of the first **girls' schools** in Pune in 1848?
practice.solution: **Savitribai Phule**, taught by and working with **Jyotirao Phule**, ran the pioneering girls' school at Bhide Wada, Pune (1848).

practice.q: The **Theosophical Society**'s international headquarters at **Adyar** (1882) is near which city?
practice.solution: The Theosophical Society (founded 1875 in New York by **Blavatsky and Olcott**) moved its headquarters to **Adyar, Madras**, in 1882; Annie Besant led it later.

practice.q: **Servants of India Society** (1905), which trained dedicated public workers, was founded by —
practice.solution: **Gokhale** founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 — he was also Gandhi's acknowledged political guru.

practice.q: The **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act** was passed in —
practice.solution: The **Widows' Remarriage Act (1856)** legalised widow remarriage — Vidyasagar's campaign. Sati was banned in 1829.

practice.q:
Arrange the reform laws chronologically:
1. Sarda Act  2. Sati abolition  3. Age of Consent Act  4. Widow Remarriage Act
practice.solution: **Sati (1829) → Widow Remarriage (1856) → Age of Consent (1891) → Sarda Act (1929)**.

practice.q: The **Age of Consent Act, 1891** raised the age of consent for girls to —
practice.solution: The **Age of Consent Act (1891)** raised it from 10 to **12** years — passed after the Rukhmabai and Phulmoni controversies.

practice.q: **Sri Narayana Guru**, who consecrated the Aruvippuram temple (1888), worked among the —
practice.solution: **Sri Narayana Guru** led the Ezhava reform movement in Kerala and inspired the **SNDP Yogam (1903)**.

practice.q: Which reform movement's motto was **'one caste, one religion, one God for man'**?
options: The movement of Sri Narayana Guru
practice.solution: **Sri Narayana Guru's** famous formulation summarised his anti-caste universalism in Kerala.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Arya Samaj launched shuddhi (reconversion) ceremonies.
2. The Singh Sabha (1873) worked for Sikh revival.
3. The Mahad Satyagraha (1927) was led by Periyar.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are right. The **Mahad Satyagraha was led by B.R. Ambedkar**, not Periyar (whose movement is the Self-Respect Movement).

practice.q: The **Indian National Congress** was founded in 1885 by —
practice.solution: **Alan Octavian Hume**, a retired ICS officer, organised the first session at Bombay in December 1885; **W.C. Bonnerjee** presided.

practice.q: How many delegates attended the **first session** of the Indian National Congress?
practice.solution: The Bombay session of **December 1885** had **72 delegates**, drawn mostly from professional classes of the presidencies.

practice.q: Who is known as the **'Grand Old Man of India'**?
practice.solution: **Naoroji** — thrice Congress president, first Indian MP in the British House of Commons (1892), author of the drain theory.

practice.q:
Consider the statements about Moderate leaders:
1. Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.
2. S.N. Banerjea founded the Indian Association in 1876.
3. R.C. Dutt wrote *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* is **Naoroji's** book; **R.C. Dutt** wrote the *Economic History of India*.
practice.shortcut: Swap the two economic books — that's the trap.

practice.q: Tilak started the public **Ganapati festival** in 1893 primarily to —
options: Build a mass base against British rule
practice.solution: The **Ganapati (1893)** and **Shivaji (1895)** festivals gave Tilak a legal platform to gather and mobilise the masses.
practice.shortcut: Festivals = political mobilisation under a religious cover.

practice.q: Tilak was sentenced to six years' imprisonment in 1908 and imprisoned at —
practice.solution: After the 1908 sedition trial over *Kesari* articles, Tilak served **1908–14 in Mandalay**, writing *Geeta Rahasya* there.

practice.q: The stated purpose of the **Partition of Bengal (1905)** was —
practice.solution: Curzon claimed the province was too big to govern; nationalists saw the real aim — splitting Bengali unity — and launched the Swadeshi movement.
practice.shortcut: Stated = administrative; real = divide the nationalists.

practice.q:
Match:
1. Rakhi bandhan as protest — Rabindranath Tagore
2. *Amar Sonar Bangla* — composed during Swadeshi agitation
3. National Council of Education — 1906
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three are Swadeshi-era facts: Tagore's Rakhi tying and later the song (now Bangladesh's anthem), and the **National Council of Education (1906)** for national education.

practice.q: The Congress split into Moderates and Extremists took place at the **Surat session** of —
practice.solution: The **1907 Surat session** (Rash Behari Ghosh's presidency disputed) split the party; the wings reunited at **Lucknow in 1916**.

practice.q: At which Congress session were the **Moderates and Extremists reunited**?
practice.solution: The **Lucknow session (1916)** saw the reunion and the **Congress-League pact** (which accepted separate electorates).

practice.q: Who among the following was the **first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council** (1909)?
practice.solution: The **Morley-Minto reforms (1909)** admitted **S.P. Sinha** (law member) to the Viceroy's Executive Council — and introduced separate electorates.
practice.shortcut: Sinha in; separate electorates in — both 1909.

practice.q:
Consider the statements about the **Home Rule Leagues (1916)**:
1. Tilak's league worked in Maharashtra, Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar.
2. Annie Besant's league had its headquarters at Adyar, Madras.
3. Both leagues demanded Dominion Status within the British Empire.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three hold: the two leagues divided the country between them (Tilak: April 1916; Besant: September 1916) and both pressed for self-government within the Empire.
practice.shortcut: Two leagues, one demand: Home Rule.

practice.q: Gandhi's **first satyagraha in India** was launched at —
practice.solution: **Champaran (Bihar), 1917**, against the tinkathia indigo system — Rajkumar Shukla had persuaded Gandhi to come.

practice.q: The **tinkathia system**, which Gandhi fought in 1917, obliged Champaran peasants to —
options: Grow indigo on 3/20 of their land
Provide free transport to indigo factories
practice.solution: **Tinkathia** forced each raiyat to cultivate indigo on the **three kathas in every twenty** of his best land.

practice.q:
Arrange chronologically:
1. Ahmedabad mill strike
2. Champaran Satyagraha
3. Kheda Satyagraha
4. Return of Gandhi to India
practice.solution: Returned **9 January 1915** → **Champaran 1917** → **Ahmedabad 1918** (mill) → **Kheda 1918** (revenue).
practice.shortcut: 15-17-18-18: return, Champaran, then the two 1918 fights.

practice.q: The **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** was carried out on the orders of —
practice.solution: Brigadier-General **Reginald Dyer** ordered the firing on 13 April 1919; O'Dwyer was the Punjab Governor — later shot dead by Udham Singh (1940).
practice.shortcut: Dyer fired; O'Dwyer backed — Udham Singh shot O'Dwyer.

practice.q: The **Rowlatt Act (1919)** is remembered as the act of —
practice.solution: The Rowlatt Act allowed arrest and detention **without trial** — no lawyer, no argument, no appeal — and was never actually used much before it was repealed.

practice.q: The **Non-Cooperation Movement** was formally withdrawn after the violence at —
practice.solution: At **Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur), 5 February 1922**, a mob set a police station ablaze; Gandhi, committed to non-violence, called off the movement.

practice.q: The **Swaraj Party** (1923), which entered the councils, was founded by —
practice.solution: After NCM's withdrawal, **C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru** formed the Swaraj Party to fight councils from within.

practice.q: How many volunteers accompanied Gandhi on the **Dandi March**?
practice.solution: Gandhi left Sabarmati on **12 March 1930 with 78 followers**, covering about 240 miles to Dandi and breaking the salt law on **6 April 1930**.

practice.q:
Match:
1. Communal Award — Ramsay MacDonald, 1932
2. Poona Pact — reserved seats under joint electorates
3. Gandhi attended the First Round Table Conference
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Gandhi attended only the **Second** RTC (1931) — the First (1930) had no Congress representative.
practice.shortcut: First RTC = no Congress; Gandhi = Second only.

practice.q: The **Nehru Report (1928)**, India's first constitution draft, was prepared under —
practice.solution: **Motilal Nehru** chaired the committee that drafted the **Nehru Report (1928)**, demanding Dominion Status — Jinnah answered with his Fourteen Points.

practice.q: **26 January 1930** is significant because —
options: The first Independence Day was observed
practice.solution: After the **Lahore Purna Swaraj resolution (Dec 1929)**, **26 January 1930** was celebrated as Independence Day — the date later chosen for the Republic (1950).

practice.q: The **Quit India** resolution was passed on 8 August 1942 at —
practice.solution: The All India Congress Committee passed Quit India at **Gowalia Tank (August Kranti Maidan), Bombay**, with Gandhi's call: **'Do or Die'**.

practice.q: The **Rani of Jhansi Regiment** of the INA was commanded by —
practice.solution: **Captain Lakshmi Sahgal** led the INA's women's regiment under Subhas Bose's Azad Hind government (1943).

practice.q:
Who among the following were the members of the **Cabinet Mission (1946)**?
1. Lord Pethick-Lawrence
2. Stafford Cripps
3. A.V. Alexander
4. Lord Wavell
practice.solution: The **Cabinet Mission** = Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State), **Cripps** and **Alexander**. Wavell was the Viceroy, not a mission member.

practice.q: ***Kesari*** and ***Mahratta***, started in 1881, were edited by —
practice.solution: **Tilak** ran *Kesari* in Marathi and *Mahratta* in English — both from Pune; his 1908 *Kesari* articles led to the Mandalay sentence.

practice.q: ***Bengalee***, the newspaper associated with the Indian Association (1876), was edited by —
practice.solution: **S.N. Banerjea** used *Bengalee* to campaign for civil rights and against the 1905 partition; he founded the Indian Association in 1876.

practice.q: Which newspaper, founded in 1868, **changed its language from Bengali to English overnight** to escape the Vernacular Press Act?
practice.solution: The **Ghosh brothers' Amrita Bazar Patrika** began as a Bengali paper (Jessore, 1868); in 1878 it converted to English overnight to dodge Lytton's gag.

practice.q: The book ***Ghulamgiri*** (Slavery, 1873) was written by —
practice.solution: **Phule's *Ghulamgiri*** attacked caste slavery and the tyranny of the 'higher' castes.

practice.q: ***The Indian Struggle* (1935)**, covering 1920–34, was written by —
practice.solution: **Bose's *The Indian Struggle*** narrated the national movement of 1920–34; the book was promptly banned in British India.

practice.q:
Match:
1. *India Wins Freedom* — Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
2. *India Divided* — Rajendra Prasad
3. *Unhappy India* — Lala Lajpat Rai
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three pairings are right: Azad's memoir, Prasad's partition critique, and Lajpat Rai's 1928 reply to *Mother India*.

practice.q: The **Vernacular Press Act (1878)** — the 'Gagging Act' — was passed by —
practice.solution: **Lytton** gagged Indian-language papers in 1878; **Ripon repealed** it in 1882.

practice.q: During the **Non-Cooperation Movement**, Gandhi's English journal was —
practice.solution: Gandhi ran ***Young India*** (English) and ***Navajivan*** (Gujarati) in the NCM years; *Harijan* began only in 1933.

practice.q: Gandhi's *Indian Opinion*, his first journal, was published from —
practice.solution: Gandhi started ***Indian Opinion*** in **1903 in South Africa**, years before his Indian journals.

practice.q: The song ***Vande Mataram*** occurs in Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel —
practice.solution: ***Anandamath* (1882)** contains Vande Mataram; Tagore first sang it at the **1896 Calcutta session** of the Congress.

practice.q: Rabindranath Tagore composed ***Amar Sonar Bangla*** during —
options: The Swadeshi movement against the 1905 partition
practice.solution: Written during the **1905 anti-partition agitation**, the song is now the national anthem of **Bangladesh**.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. *Hind Swaraj* was written by Gandhi in 1909.
2. *Geeta Rahasya* was composed by Tilak in prison.
3. *Annihilation of Caste* was an undelivered speech of Nehru.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: *Annihilation of Caste* (1936) is **Ambedkar's** undelivered address to the Jat-Pat-Todak Mandal, not Nehru's.

practice.q: Which Governor-General is called the **'liberator of the Indian press'**?
practice.solution: **Charles Metcalfe** removed press restrictions in 1835 — press freedom stayed until the 1878 Act; Ripon later repealed that Act.
practice.shortcut: Metcalfe 1835 liberates; Lytton 1878 gags; Ripon 1882 repeals.
